Donghae Motors Announces Major Expansion of Electric Vehicle Plant in Ulsan

Donghae Motors has unveiled plans to significantly expand its electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing facility in Ulsan, South Korea, reflecting rising global demand for cleaner transportation and the country’s push to strengthen its role in the automotive transition.

The company disclosed on Wednesday that it will invest approximately 420 billion won ($305 million) over the next two years to enlarge its current plant, increasing annual production capacity from 60,000 to 100,000 EV units. Construction is set to begin in the third quarter of this year, with the expanded facility expected to be operational by early 2026.

“We are responding to robust market momentum for electric vehicles both domestically and internationally,” said Donghae Motors CEO Kim Min-jun during the announcement. “This investment underscores our commitment to sustainable mobility and to the Ulsan community, which remains central to our operations.”

The expansion is projected to create around 400 jobs in the region, according to a statement from the Ulsan city government. “Donghae’s investment further consolidates Ulsan’s position as a leading automotive hub in East Asia,” said Park Ji-hoon, Director of Industrial Development for Ulsan.

Industry analysts note that South Korea’s automotive sector has seen a surge in EV-related investments, driven by international emissions regulations and domestic incentives. The Korea Automobile Manufacturers Association welcomed the announcement, calling it a “positive signal for the sector’s competitiveness and supply chain resilience.”

Donghae Motors reported that the expanded facility will utilize advanced automation and energy-efficient technologies, aligning with national targets for carbon neutrality. Local suppliers are also expected to benefit from increased procurement contracts as Donghae ramps up output.

With the move, Donghae Motors aims to strengthen its export footprint and meet growing demand in Europe and Southeast Asia, according to company officials.
